title: Check If Digits Are Equal in String After Operations I
statement:
`s` is a string of decimal digits. One round replaces `s` with the new digits `(s[i] + s[i + 1]) mod 10` for every neighbouring pair, taken from left to right (`i = 0, 1, ..., s.length - 2`), so each round makes the string one digit shorter.

Keep doing rounds until exactly two digits remain. Return `true` if those two digits are equal, and `false` if they differ.
constraints: s contains only the digits 0 to 9
notes:
## Intuition

The rules describe exactly what to compute, and the string is short (at most 100 digits), so the plain simulation is the intended solution: about `n² / 2` additions in total. Each round only needs the previous round's digits, and it can even overwrite them in place: the new digit at `i` uses the old digits at `i` and `i + 1`, and going left to right, the one at `i + 1` has not been overwritten yet.

(Each final digit turns out to be the original digits weighted by a row of Pascal's triangle, modulo 10. That shortcut matters only in the harder version of this problem, where `s` is much longer.)

## Approach

1. Turn `s` into an array of numbers, `digits`.
2. Let `length` be the number of digits still in play. While it is more than 2, run one round.
3. In a round, for `i` from 0 to `length - 2`, set `digits[i]` to `(digits[i] + digits[i + 1]) % 10`. The last digit of the round is now stale and drops out as `length` shrinks by one.
4. When two digits remain, return whether `digits[0]` equals `digits[1]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`digits = [3, 9, 0, 2]`.

- `length = 4`: `3 + 9 → 2`, `9 + 0 → 9`, `0 + 2 → 2`, giving `[2, 9, 2]` (plus the stale 2).
- `length = 3`: `2 + 9 → 1`, `9 + 2 → 1`, giving `[1, 1]`.
- `length = 2`: stop. `1 === 1`, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): `n - 2` rounds of at most `n - 1` additions.
- Space: O(n) for `digits`.

## Pitfalls

- Stop at two digits, not one.
- Keep only the last digit of each sum (`% 10`); a carry is not passed on.
- If you overwrite in place, go left to right; right to left would read digits already replaced in this round.
- Compare numbers with numbers: in JavaScript, `s[0] + s[1]` joins two characters into a string.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `digits` | the current digits; only the first `length` are in play |
| `length` | how many digits remain before this round |
| `i` | position of the left digit of the pair being added |

narration.2: Turn the characters into numbers so they can be added.
narration.3: All the digits are in play at the start.
narration.4: Each pass of this loop is one round; rounds continue until two digits remain.
narration.5: Visit every neighbouring pair among the digits still in play.
narration.6: Replace the left digit by the last digit of the pair's sum; the right one still holds its old value, so overwriting is safe.
narration.8: The round produced one digit fewer, so the last position drops out.
narration.10: Two digits remain: the answer is whether they are equal.
